items.title: Bobby Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: then I’m playing with a group called Hal Smith’s Roadrunners

ctx.x: Back to San Diego and to start my weekend job, then I’m playing with a group called Hal Smith’s Roadrunners, and we’re going to be, next month, a couple of weeks from now, two or three weeks from now we’re going to be in Sun Valley Idaho playing a jazz festival up there, and I’m looking forward to that, then we go to Scottsdale and then Palm Springs. I’m playing a date with the Palm Springs Symphony Orchestra, and then I’m playing here and there and then doing some more recordings. I’ve just had three recordings…
How does that work with jazz recording these days? You know downstairs they have a whole slew of CDs and many, many record labels. Do they call you? Or do you actively promote yourself to them?

items.title: Hal Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: So when I, for instance with the Road Runners, Bobby Gordon’s got his regular job in San Diego and now it’s only two nights a week.

ctx.x: You’ve done quite a bit of band leading. What’s the biggest headache in being a band leader? The biggest thing to surmount?

Coordinating everyone’s schedules. Because nobody can give their loyalty to one band. So when I, for instance with the Road Runners, Bobby Gordon’s got his regular job in San Diego and now it’s only two nights a week. But he also works with Marty Grosz and the Orphan Newsboys, and plays jazz parties as a solo. So I’ve got to coordinate that. Rebecca works all the time in Portland, freelance and with Dave Frishberg, and she’s on this jazz party circuit. So that’s enough right there. Then the other two guys are…
And now you’re going to be even more spread out, because you’re going to be in New Orleans.
